messages.text: Do you still want those wide-mouth lids from Dollar General? I can pick up two boxes before I come Thursday.
Yes please. I used more than I meant to last year on the tomato pieces and the peach halves.
I will get them. Also Mr. Wade said his fig tree gave him too many for the freezer, so I told him you might know what to do with a sack.
Tell him not too big a sack. Four little jars is plenty for Frank and me.
Call me when you sit down. I keep thinking about Agnes and that hospital room.
I will in a bit. I put the kettle on and went back to those blue fabric squares Mama would have fussed over.
That sounds like her. She would make you pick out every crooked corner before supper.
I only fixed two corners, but my hands are steadier now. I will ring you before nine.
Before you leave, where did you put the church kitchen envelopes?
Top drawer by the stamps. I am dropping them off after I check on Mrs. Hanley.
You still want me to warm up the leftovers instead of buying lunch out?
Yes. We have plenty here, and I will be back before your sugar check.
Do you want me to set the cooler by the back door before I go out?
Yes, please. I have chicken rice for Gene and a small pan for the Harris boys after school.
I put the blue ice packs in. Gene still at the house this morning?
He said noon is fine. Linda will sit with Martha while I run it over.
Mama, boys' game got moved to March 21 at 2. You want me to text it again closer?
I put March 21, 2:00, under the magnet on the fridge so your daddy will see it too.
Good. I know you like it where you can point at it.
Yes, and I wrote your visit list in the little spiral by the phone. Faucet washer, porch bulb, and Frank's mower belt.
Mom, did you see that link Uncle Ray sent about the drops for blood sugar? He asked me if Dad wanted the order page.
Mama, do you still have Grandma's biscuit card? Jenny wants to try it for the boys Saturday.
Tell him Frank and I are staying with Dr. Patel's paper and the pharmacy sheet. I am not clicking that order button.
It is tucked in the green tin with the little song sheets from Oak Grove. I will take a picture after supper.
Good. I will leave it alone. Boys are asking if Pop is watching Braves tonight.
No rush. Dad said you were sewing on that blue cover again.
He has it on already. Send a picture after practice and ignore Ray if he keeps pushing it.
Saw the plant had that shutdown today. You sent just 'fine,' so I figured you were taking your minute. I can call Sunday after supper if that suits.
Just mending the corner before I bring it Sunday. Your grandmama's stitches are still stronger than mine.
It was a mess. I'm home now. Boys are fed.
Good. I wrote down the porch rail, Frank's mower blade, and the boys' shoe sizes so I do not keep asking you twice.
Send the rail picture. I'll bring tools when we come.
You still up? I can't get settled tonight.
I'm right here. Frank's already down. Call me when you sit down.
Give me five minutes to heat the kettle. Griffin's quiet tonight, just the dog fussing at the porch.
Take your time, sister. I'm not going anywhere.
I put both health cards in the blue folder before we leave. Please do not set your coffee on it.
Paula said she can only talk around noon, after the morning desk rush settles.
It is on the hall table. I will carry it.
That is fine. I will call her after we get back from Kroger.
After the clinic, I want to stop at Kroger and ask why that refill is $14 there and $26 at CVS.
Mark sent that picture from the ball field. Two muddy uniforms and everybody smiling.
Save it for me. I want to see those boys before his Sunday call.
Alright. We can swing by the eye place too if your left frame keeps slipping.
Iris, I put you on the meal table for 10:30 to noon Saturday, not the doorway greeting. Will that suit you better?
That helps. I can do labels and envelopes sitting down. My right knee has been fussy before noon, and my fingers do better after warm water.
Good. I will ask Helen to handle the front steps and I will save you the chair by the coffee urn.
Thank you. Frank and I are also trying the county office next Tuesday morning so I am not standing in that big line later.
We may come through Saturday after the boys' practice. Need me to bring anything from here?
No, I have enough here. I pulled a bag of vegetables from the freezer and set beans to soak for tomorrow.
That will work. Dad said he can look at that loose cabinet hinge while I am there.
Good. If the peaches thaw right, I may put a small pan in the oven after supper.
Mama, that tire place by the courthouse still does Tuesday paperwork prices if y'all show the card at the desk.
I put that card in the bill folder after church, so I will take it with the tire receipt.
Good. If the tread can wait, I can look at it when we come through.
We are waiting on the back two. I wrote it in my March notebook beside the grocery slips.
Mama, the boys want to know if Papa still has that picture of you two by the '74 Chevy.
He has it in the hall drawer with Paula's baby bracelet and your little league picture.
Send it when you can. I told Caleb and Jonah that Papa's hair used to be darker than mine.
I will. Tell those boys I found the Braves cards too, one for each of them and the girls.
Mama, the boys brought home a brochure from school with old paddlewheel boats on it. Made me think of you.
Set it aside if it has the Natchez stop on there. I like the ones where folks sit and watch the banks go by.
Mama, the boys asked why you don't put those candidate signs by the mailbox like some folks do.
Tell them their Granny keeps the mailbox for bills and birthday cards. I save that kind of talk for the kitchen table with people who won't holler.
This one says Memphis down toward New Orleans. Not a bus every morning kind of thing.
Fair enough. They hear enough hollering at ball practice.
That sounds more my speed. I put a little extra in the blue envelope after groceries this week.
And I want them to learn to ask questions without making enemies. They're growing up with more to sort through than we did.
Mama, did you see the county article I sent? The part about cameras on every shift was buried halfway down.
I read it after supper. I marked that and the part about more practice before things get loud.
That is the part I wanted you to notice. Some folks are going downtown Saturday.
I am going to stay here and talk it through with you and Carol. Crowds wear me out, but I do want to understand it plain.
Sister, I was sorting through Mama's tin and found that picture of us out by the chicken coop on the Newton road place. You couldn't have been more than seven.
Lord, that old place. Daddy still had the tractor with the busted seat back then. I want to say that was the summer before you started first grade.
Mhm. Remember walking the dirt road to Mt. Pleasant for Sunday school? Our shoes stayed dusty all summer long.
Every blessed Sunday. Mama wouldn't hear of skipping even when the well water tasted like iron. Send me that picture when you get a minute.
Did you see the squash casserole Mae put up? I wrote down half of it but missed the oven part.
I saw it after supper when I made my second pass through the blue app. It said 350 for 35 minutes.
Good. Send it to me tomorrow if you can. Also check the church page, Linda said they changed the serving time.
I saved both. I will look once more in the morning before I call you.
Credit union shows the two regular deposits came in. I wrote the balances on the yellow pad.
Good. I will sort the receipts after breakfast and we can take the light bill over before lunch.
No rush. Braves replay is on at ten if you want coffee first.
Coffee first sounds right. The bank can wait until the traffic thins.
Mama, the portal posted your visit summary. Want me to print the refill page before I leave work?
Yes please. Dr. Patel said keep the little white tablet at breakfast and write down the morning numbers for two weeks.
I will bring it Sunday. Please do not change anything because of that article Aunt Carol sent.
I won't. I put on the kettle with ginger and lemon, but I am leaving the tablet schedule just like she wrote it.
Ground is still wet out back. I put your blue shoes by the kitchen door.
Thank you. I will take the short way around and just look at the roses and feeders.
Good. Tomatoes can wait if it starts misting again.
When you go by Kroger, see if bread is still $2.99. I am keeping the county sheet on the table so we can finish it after lunch.
I will look. Also the detour sign is still up by Flat Shoals.
That is the stretch I wrote beside the commission names. Too many folks speeding past that school.
I will take the back way home and check the price on eggs too.
Daddy got the Atlanta game pulled up yet? Boys asked if he is keeping score in that old notebook.
He is already in his chair with the pencil. I told him supper can wait till the fifth inning.
Tell him we saw the New Orleans schedule talk this morning. I will call Sunday if he wants to fuss about it.
He will. I keep up better once the weather turns and those games start meaning something.
Did that lady at the center show you how to make the letters bigger?
She did, and I can read your biscuit note now without hunting for my glasses.
Good. Can you send it to my email too? My printer likes that better.
I just sent it. Tell me if it lands right.
You still up? I put my Sunday papers away early tonight so they wouldn't stare at me from the table.
I was just looking at the Piedmont envelope again and then checking whether I locked the back door.
Call me when you sit down. We can talk about biscuits or Mama's old quilt, anything but papers.
I'll call in a minute. Frank fell asleep with the Braves recap on, so the house got too still.
I set the tomatoes by the back door. Take the soft ones first.
I will carry a few to Mr. Wallace after lunch. I need to ring Mrs. Carter too before she starts worrying about that porch rail.
Tell her I can look at it Tuesday if she wants. I put the screwdriver back in the drawer.
Thank you. I will ask when she answers, then I will step across the street with the tomatoes.
I saved you the seat beside me for Wednesday supper, but there may be nearly forty signed up.
That is kind of you. I may just help drop off the rolls and slip home after.
That is perfectly fine. Ruth asked whether you, she, and Miss Evelyn might do coffee after your Tuesday pages instead.
That sounds easier. Four chairs at Ruth's kitchen table would suit me better.
I have the soup names from Ruth Ann and Betty. Do you still have the paper sheet for Thursday supper?
Yes, it is in my blue folder. I added Mrs. Hollis for a ride and left two blank lines for anyone who calls tomorrow.
Good. I will ask June to handle the coffee table so you are not there from morning till dark.
Thank you. I can do the calls and the sheet, but I am going home after the pans are labeled.
I can bring my drill when we come through Saturday. Need anything besides that rail by the back steps?
If you have room, bring those long gloves too. The rose canes are waking up and I cannot wrestle the old ones like I used to.
I will trim the heavy stuff and check that loose board by the shed.
Thank you. Your daddy can hold the flashlight, but I would rather you handle the ladder.
I can look at that back porch rail when we come through next time. Same side by the kitchen?
Yes, the side where your daddy put those extra boards after that bad storm years ago.
Okay. The boys still talk about that narrow hallway at y'all's place in Covington.
Tell them their room is ready when they visit, even if it is mostly quilts and photo boxes now.
Morning. You feeling any better than Friday? I've been thinking about you since we talked Sunday.
A little. Knees were stiff getting out of bed but the coffee helped.
Good. I tried that buttermilk biscuit you sent me Tuesday, came out flat. I'll show you when I drive up on the 28th.
Bring the recipe card and we'll fix it together. I'll have greens going.
Found that picture of mama's people standing by the tobacco barn in '48. All seven of them lined up.
Lord, look at those faces. Aunt Lurleen looks just like you do now.
Mama wrote 'Whitley reunion 1948' on the back in pencil.
Save it for the binder. I'll bring the Trujillo side photos too, the ones Frank's cousin sent last fall, so both branches are in there.
Call me when you sit down. That afternoon sounded like too much.
I am better now. I went out back with the little clippers and took the brown tops off the roses.
That usually settles you. Did those tomato cups on the sill perk up any?
They did, and the redbirds emptied the porch tube again. Frank says they eat like company.
I put the State Farm envelope by your notebook.
Thank you. That one and Dr. Nash's bill made February look too big, right around 3200 on my adding machine.
March ought to settle back down if the truck behaves.
I hope so. I wrote 2700 to 2900 on the side so I do not fuss over one odd page.
Mama, I found the page you asked about. I am printing the plain one from cdc.gov and circling the part about timing.
Thank you. I can read it better on paper than on this phone.
I will drop it by after work. You can take it with you when you ask at the counter.
That will help. I want to hear what Mr. Henson says with the paper in hand.
Martha squeezed my hand twice today and tried three words with the therapist.
I am thankful for that. I kept busy with a potato casserole and then sat quiet a minute.
Gene ate the soup you brought and said the cornbread helped more than he expected.
I will make another pot Friday. Call me after supper if you need to talk.
Mama, the form for the senior center wants the highest grade you finished. I'm filling out yours and Daddy's together so don't make me guess.
Twelfth, honey. Newton High, graduated in '69. Daddy needed me at home after that. You know I always wished I'd gone on but life had its own ideas.
Daddy says put his as eleventh, he never finished the last year. I'll tell them no degree past high school for either of y'all.
That's right. Mark the box honest. They don't need a fancy story from us.
Call me when you sit down. Did the cold make your knees act up today?
A little, so I kept my rounds slow. The basil looks fine, but one rose cane needs tying.
Do not fool with it too long. I know you like to get those things seen to before the day gets away.
I was already back inside with coffee by then.
Did you find that notice from the insurance people? Mine was tucked behind a recipe card somehow.
Found it. It was in the blue folder with Frank's last bill and the prescription list Paula helped me mark.
Good. I have to lay mine out on the table or I forget what I already checked.
Same here. When Paula sends a screen picture, I still write the date on the corner before I tuck it away.
Did that cough ease any? I still say honey and lemon before bed helps me settle.
It did soothe it some. I used that and the heating pad while Frank watched the Braves.
Good. You still calling Dr. Patel's office in the morning like you said?
Yes, especially since she changed my refill last week. I want her nurse to tell me what to do.
They moved it to 8:20.
I saw. You have been on the porch with that coffee a long while, so I put the questions on the yellow pad and packed crackers.
I'm alright. Truck has gas.
Then we will go early, sit near the side door, and come straight home. I already set your supper plate in the fridge.
The ladies' ministry note is up now. Mrs. Hanley needs soup on Tuesday instead of Monday.
Thank you. I had just opened the feed after breakfast and saw the prayer request but not the meal change.
It may be under announcements. The garden group posted pretty azaleas too, if you want a happier thing to see.
I will look there before I close it. Frank is ready for the grocery run.
Iris, would you bring the old red folder tonight? We are short on the second verse for Mrs. Evans's favorite.
I can. It has Mama's notes in the margin, so I always check twice before lending it out.
I understand. I will keep it with me and hand it right back after practice.
Thank you. I will also bring the lemon loaf recipe for the meal list.
Are you still riding over at 6? Mae said lane 4 has the wobbly chair again.
Yes, Frank will drop me by the doors. I told them not to put me beside that chair unless they want me fussing all evening.
Dottie is bringing her lemon drops and already warned me she may not hit a thing.
That is usually when we have the best time. I will bring napkins for the candy bowl.
Mom, can I bring Ethan's baseball pants next weekend? Knee is torn again.
Bring them. Tell him not to wash them with gum in the pocket this time.
I will. You still have that heavy denim piece Dad gave you?
Yes, and Mama's thimble too. I was already at the machine with my green-and-white blocks when your message came.
Mom, we found six of your empty jars in the garage from Christmas. Want me to bring them next time?
Bring them if it is no trouble. The tall ones work better for tomatoes, and the short ones are good when peaches are soft.
Okay. Boys asked if you still make the sweet brown stuff they had on biscuits.
Only when somebody gives me figs. I do not go hunting for them.
Mama, I can call Sunday after supper. Need me to look at that porch rail when we come through?
Yes, if you do not mind. I will be here all day Monday too, so whatever time suits y'all.
Okay. Paula said you were checking papers from the credit union. Everything line up?
It lined up. Just the usual two deposits and the insurance draft, nothing extra to chase down.
Mom the patient portal pulled the wrong box on your demographics again. Same one as last visit.
Lord have mercy. Tell them to set it to match daddy's intake from January and leave it.
Will do. I'm pretty sure the new system is auto-filling off the surname field. Front desk said it happens whenever a chart gets migrated.
Third time this year. Nobody ever checked that box wrong back when I was a Whitley.
Mama, I printed the sample ballot for you. Want me to mark the sections about clinic funding and prescription caps?
Yes, those matter to me and Frank. But leave the rest plain so I can read it myself after supper.
I know. You like parts from both stacks and dislike the loud flyers from both.
That sounds about right. Some old ways still sit with me, but the doctor bills and the folks on fixed checks are real too.
That cousin sent me the steam bath thing again and then started fussing about the county board. I closed my phone.
I would have too. Paula can find the real page if we need it, and I am not spending my morning in that back-and-forth.
Call me after breakfast. I want your lighter biscuit note, not all that mess.
Did your collards make it through that cold snap?
Enough for one pot. I cut the best leaves this morning and will cook them down with onion.
That sounds good. I still have a jar of tomatoes from last week if you need it.
Thank you, but I found two cans in the cabinet and Frank asked for cornbread with it.
I found the county paper under the Braves schedule. It only needs filing with the insurance sheet.
Good. Put it in the blue house folder before Paula stops by after work.
Done. I left room for the termite receipt too.
Thank you. After she leaves, it will be quiet enough for us to watch the first inning.
I am at Ingles. The cereal rings up lower with the paper slips, but the ham does not.
Get the cereal and leave the ham. We have beans, greens, and chicken thighs for two suppers.
Cashier asked if I wanted the Tuesday button too. I told her to try it.
If it changes the total, take it. I will mark the new number in the notebook.
We made it back before dark. Boys ate half the pantry after practice.
I figured they would. Tell them Nana saw the picture and loved it.
Boys made it home from practice. You and Dad need anything before Sunday call?
Will do. Paula texted me about that paper you needed signed. She said send her a photo if the print is too small.
She is good with those forms. I will wait until she is off that front counter.
No, son. I made a note by the bed so I won't get up twice wondering if I mailed the insurance form.
Good. Put it by the coffee pot too. Dad watching the game?
Yes. My checkup paper just says usual follow-up and sleep notes, so nothing new to tell you.
Mama, did y'all get in and out Tuesday? The office crowd looked bigger when I drove past at lunch.
We were done before the lunch rush. Frank dropped me close, and I only had to wait behind four people.
Good. Please keep doing the short trips like that. Those long church mornings take it out of you.
I know. I told Linda I will help with envelopes and phone calls, but no more standing by the hall for two hours.
Did Paula send you that video from the town meeting? I watched ten minutes and had to pause it.
She did. I wrote down where the woman asked what happens after a bad stop gets reported.
That question stuck with me too. Call me when you sit down and we can compare notes.
I will. I would rather hear it quiet with you than stand in all that shouting outside the square.
Did you ever hear from that downtown office again after they wanted you there every weekday?
Only years ago. I remember thinking I could not be gone that many afternoons with children coming in hungry.
Mama needed rides then too. You always had three places pulling on you.
Those little school cafeteria hours fit better. We paid bills, kept supper on, and nobody had to wait long.
I set the recorder for the 1:05 Atlanta game. Remote is on your side table.
Thank you. I will finish folding towels before the first pitch.
Also kept that black-and-gold preview from last night. Might watch it after supper.
That sounds fine if I do not fall asleep in the recliner.
Miss Evelyn did not make it to the luncheon. I left a plate with Jean.
I will call her before supper. If she needs milk, I can add it when I carry biscuits to the Browns.
That would be kind. I am trying not to add one more stop before Bible study.
You go on and rest your feet. I have the Browns' number if their gate is latched.
Boys are asking if you can do the little screen call after supper.
Yes, I found the green camera button where the fellow showed us Wednesday.
If it acts up, just text me. I will walk you through it.
I will. I also moved that Braves photo into the family group like you told me.
Boys said their bus was late twice this week. Y'all still got that road work near the church?
Yes, and I underlined the transportation part on the school board mailer. They need to hear about buses and that narrow sidewalk.
Makes sense. Dad watching the Braves?
He is. I am saving the sheriff card for after the seventh inning so we can read the answers together.
Mama, bring that cream folder Sunday. I can sort the insurance papers after lunch.
Thank you. Frank said he will carry the box with the old pictures so I do not fuss with it.
Good. Maddie and Elise want the picture where you and Daddy are standing by the first little house.
I know the one. It is near your hospital bracelet and Mark's school papers.
Mama, when you go Monday, ask them to run both cards before you pay. Sometimes the second one does not get entered.
I wrote that on the envelope. I also wrote to ask if the small white tablet comes in the lower-price bottle.
Good. Take the eye estimate too. I can call after work if the number still looks high.
Thank you, honey. The scratch on these lenses is right where I read.
Did your lilies show yet? Mine have little points all along the fence.
Yes, the bed near the kitchen window has little green spears. I sat on the top step and pulled what I could reach.
Do not overdo it. Let Frank or one of the children get the low weeds.
Paula said she may stop after church next Sunday, and I saved the doctor papers for her to read at the table.
I am heading to the shed before church. Did you put Paula's papers in your purse?
Yes, in the side pocket with my glasses.
Good. We can swing by Covington Drug after lunch if you still want to ask him.
I do. He has kept up with our medicines long enough to know what we mean.
I can bring the church pan by after lunch if that still helps.
Thank you. I will be outside a few minutes first, tying the beans and pinching basil before we leave.
Take your time. I saw two finches waiting on your rail yesterday like they owned it.
They were early again today. I put fresh seed out before coffee and left the broom by the steps.
Mama, did you want me to help read that dental statement when I come by after work?
Yes, please. Between that and the car paper last month, my little total sat near 3200.
Bring the blue folder too. I can separate the one-time things from the regular stack.
I have the regular stack marked 2700 to 2900 so I can see the difference.
Mama, I found the page you asked about. The smaller boat has two nights in Vicksburg and says seating is reserved for supper.
I like the sound of not standing in lines. Does it show a place to sit outside without a lot of stairs?
Yes ma'am. I can print that part and the payment schedule when I leave work.
Print the slowest one. I will keep folding a little cash away and not count on it too hard.
Mama, did Aunt Carol get her pulmonology appointment moved? She said it was still showing the 30th.
She told me last night on the phone they pushed it to April 6 in Griffin. I'll ride down that morning if Frank's feeling up to it.
Good. She listens to you. Y'all talk more than me and my sister do in a year.
We always have. I called her first thing when Linda's news came through too.
Call me when you sit down. I can hear it in your typing.
I am in the sewing room. I pulled out the green squares and wrote tomorrow's three errands so they stop circling.
Good. Put the kettle on and tell me about it.
I will. Frank just nodded and went to check the back door twice, so I am letting him be for a little bit.
Do you want me to move the voter-guide copies off the Bible study table tonight? Betty and Harold already got sharp with each other Sunday.
Please do. We can keep the table for prayer cards and the casserole list. I don't want anybody leaving sore before the lesson starts.
I will tuck them by the office door. Folks can take one quietly if they want.
Thank you. I can read one at home with Frank after the Braves, where nobody feels they have to win the room.
Mama, did you get home before the rain? You sounded worn out after you told me about Martha's stairs.
I did. It shook me seeing Gene measure for a rail and her chair still by the kitchen table.
Please rest before you start another pan of anything.
I will sit first. Then I promised Linda two small pans for the Wednesday list.
Call me when you sit down. Did you get through all those names at the center?
I got through six and wrote two for tomorrow. I am resting before I go by First Baptist at 4.
Do not let them hand you the whole supper again.
I already told Linda I will bring the list and make the reminder calls, but Nell has the rolls and Edna has the pies.
Did you ever find Aunt Mae's collard note with the vinegar crossed out?
Yes, it was inside Daddy's old songbook, of all places. I pressed it flat and put it back in plastic.
That sounds like our house. Food notes stuck in with Sunday pages.
I smiled at the grease spot on the corner. It took me right back to her kitchen window boxes.
Call me when you sit down. Did the church ladies fuss about you skipping the pantry shift?
Nobody fussed. Linda moved me to reminder calls. I can hold the phone easier than those canned boxes.
That is sensible. Put your hands in warm water first and let Frank carry anything heavier than a Bible.
He already did. Same reason I liked going to Usher Street last week before folks lined up.
You going to your Thursday pins thing tonight?
If my knee behaves. I already set out the soft shoes and my blue sweater.
Tell them boys here said don't let Mama throw gutter balls all night.
I will tell them, and they will laugh harder than they aim.
Mama, I sent the portal note with the new refill date. It says April 6.
I saw it. I put April 6 on the fridge and on the back page of the medicine list.
That works. Bring that list Monday and the insurance letter with the green stripe.
They are clipped together now so I do not have to hunt on the phone in the waiting room.
Did you get that refill picked up or are you waiting for the other store to call?
Waiting. Walgreens said $31, Kroger said $18 if Dr. Lee signs the change.
That is a big difference. Do not keep squinting over your Bible, though.
I know. I put the eye place paper under the light bill so I remember what we can do this month.
Coffee's on. I found your blue folder on the dryer.
Thank you. I got up at 2 and moved it there so I would remember the receipt.
I put the receipt with the others. Sit with me a minute before we start running around.
I will. The nurse's note only asked me to track bedtime and keep the March 31 follow-up.
Mrs. Allen asked if you had any extra jars for the meal table Saturday. Nothing fancy.
I can spare two peach pints and maybe one tomato quart if Frank has not opened it.
That is plenty, thank you. Wade also left a grocery bag of figs in the church fridge with your name on it.
Oh mercy. I will bring little jars tomorrow and make a few for the biscuit table.
I left the meal list on your porch. Please do not take two casseroles again this week.
I promise. I am staying home this afternoon with the little red triangles and a cup of tea.
Good. Your hands need quiet work after all those phone calls.
Quiet work and Mama's small scissors. They still make the cleanest point.
The church van lunch is Thursday at 11:30. They said bring ID if you want the smaller ticket at the counter.
Thank you. Frank and I will decide at the register. If it is only pennies, I will not hold the line.
That sounds like you. I am bringing soup mix for the pantry shelf if you want one.
Yes, please. The April page is tight since the plumber, so soup mix will help.
Need me to fix anything when we come through next weekend?
Maybe the bathroom shelf. I need room for the cuff, the pill sorter, and Frank's strips without everything falling.
I can do that. You feeling okay after the refill change?
So far. I am taking it with toast like Dr. Patel wrote, and using the Epsom soak tonight for my legs.
Hey ma. Boys want to do that drive down to Eulalie's over spring break.
She'd love that. She found your great-grandpapa's marriage book from the old church up in St. Martinville.
Cool. Boys haven't ever seen where the Trujillo side actually started out.
Tell them your grandpapa was the last one born down in that parish before his folks came up to Georgia and met daddy's mama.
Mama, the page you asked about is from the county health department. I sent you that one and the CDC page.
I have ten minutes before the next check-in wave. Did Daddy find the insurance letter?
Thank you. I deleted the one with the blinking red letters and the bottle picture.
He did. It was under the Braves schedule.
Good. Mark said they may come over after Easter if his crew can cover that Friday and the boys do not have a game.
That would make Frank happy. It is a longer ride for them than for you.
Good. Also, do not answer the man in the comments asking folks to message him for half-price boxes.
I already backed out. I have no business giving him my name or card.
Are you going to that church fish fry tonight? They said the fellowship hall will be packed.
I told Linda I would send a cake but not stay through the whole thing.
That sounds like you. Will Ruth and Miss Evelyn come by before your Tuesday reading notes?
Yes, just them and Linda for tea if everyone is able.
For Mrs. Nance's family Monday, would you rather bring a vegetable pot or something sweet?
I can do the vegetable pot. The little row by the fence gave me enough mustard leaves.
That will help. I have chicken soup covered if you want to save your pecans.
I may use just a cup for a small pie. The rest can wait until the grandchildren come.
I saved you a seat for Bible study tomorrow. Also, Mr. Daniels said the next community room meeting is Thursday at 6.
Thank you. I may not go Thursday, but I want to hear what they say about those small cameras and who checks the complaints.
I understand. I can bring the handout Sunday if they give one. We can talk after coffee.
I can bring the tax copy from Conyers on Tuesday. Do you and Dad still keep everything in that blue folder?
We do. It is in the hall cabinet with the old closing papers and the roof receipts.
I'll check it after work, then head back before traffic gets heavy.
That is fine. Frank and I will have supper early, so come straight in when you get here.
I put the birthday pictures where Aunt Carol can see them. Let me know if Dad likes the one with all three boys.
I will show him after the dishes. That is when I usually make my evening look through there.
Also the Covington page has a post about that water-main work near Elm Street.
Good to know. I will check that before we plan Monday errands.
Did Frank ever find that recipe card Mama wrote for your first kitchen?
He found it behind the church directory from 1975. Paula laughed at my old handwriting.
Save me a copy. Are Mark's boys coming when Paula brings her girls?
That is the plan if Mark can get off work. I am making enough biscuits for all four young ones.
I moved your blue envelope off the table so it would not get mixed with coupons.
Thank you. I laid the river pages beside it because Paula said the quiet cabins go first.
We are not doing anything with three stops before lunch.
No, sir. If we ever go, I want rocking chairs, supper at one table, and time to look at the water.
I moved the casserole list to Thursday. Can you still make the calls, or is that too much this week?
I can call after lunch. Since I do not have a time clock anymore, mornings are easier for errands.
Thank you. I will leave the church key under the office mat like usual.
That works. I will take Frank to the pharmacy first and then head over.
Iris, the women's circle wants to put a little note in the bulletin for the September birthdays. I told them you'd be turning 75 this year. Is that right?
That's right, Linda. The 18th. Hard to believe. Frank teases me that I caught up with him again for a few months.
Bless you. I'll put it down. Pastor mentioned the ones who grew up around here — said he was going to read the towns folks were born in. You were Macon, weren't you?
Bibb County hospital, yes. Mama and Daddy moved us out to the farm in Newton before I started school though, so Covington's the only home I really remember.
Boys asked if y'all still need me to fix that loose hook by the porch when we come.
Yes, please. It is holding the green tube crooked, and the seed spills when the squirrels bump it.
I'll bring the drill. Anything else outside?
Maybe the hose by the tomato bed. I pulled weeds there after the insurance letter and forgot to coil it back.
Iris, do you still have that sheet Paula printed? Martha asked me what site it came from.
It has cdc.gov at the top. Paula said not to use the long comment pages people keep sending around.
That sounds wise. I will tell Martha to ask her own doctor too.
Please do. I still want Mr. Henson to look at mine before Frank and I choose a day.
Mama, I printed the form. Do you want me to bring it by after work?
Yes, please. I have chicken in the oven, peas soaking, and Mrs. Ellis's card by the Bible so I do not forget to mail it.
You are doing too much again. Let me take the card and the form.
I will hand them to you. Mark answered with one word about work, so I will wait until Sunday and ask him while the boys are around.
Cousin Wanda called asking what year you finished up at Newton. Her grandson is doing one of those family tree projects.
Spring of '69. Tell her I walked across that stage and was back chopping field peas by Monday morning. No further schooling after that, just work and then marriage to Frank the next year.
Same as me — I finished in '73 and that was the end of books for me too. None of us girls in our row had the money or the notion for anything past that.
That's how it was for white country folks in our part of the county back then. We were lucky Daddy let us finish twelfth at all.

Pastor Greg's new wife asked me yesterday if you and Frank speak Spanish at home. Bless her heart. I told her no, it's his family name from way back, and you both grew up Baptist out of Newton County.
She won't be the first. People hear the name and guess. Frank got it at the bank too last month.
I told her your mama Whitley was as Covington as they come, and we sang in the same youth choir at First Baptist in '67. That settled it.
Frank's grandfather is the one who carried that name down out of Louisiana. Most of his people went to Mass, not chapel. Different world from how I came up.
Mama, I saw the storms passed Covington. Did you still get outside before your shower?
Yes, just enough to make my usual circle and set the feeder straight. The tomatoes did not blow over.
Good. Please do not stay out there pulling on anything heavy before breakfast.
I did not. I only pinched a few herbs and came back in.
Did your church list settle down any this week?
Some. I sent broccoli chicken to the Millers, beans to Mrs. Epps, and broth over to Gene.
That is a lot, Iris. Is Martha able to come to the table yet?
Not without help. I say my words while the pot simmers, then I do the next small thing.
Call me when you sit down. Earl brought up the courthouse races at supper and I thought of Daddy's old kitchen table.
I remember that table too. We heard plenty one way growing up, but these young ones ask things we never asked.
Mine sure do. They don't let a person get by with just saying that's how it has always been.
Good for them, mostly. I still hold to some of what Mama taught, but I can't fuss against help for medicine or old folks keeping the lights on.
Bank shows both checks now.
Good. I will copy the 3600 before the little take-outs, same as I did on the first page.
Want me to hold off on the hardware store?
Power bill came. I left it by your coffee.
Just until I finish the column. If we stay near the 2800 mark, we are all right.
Thank you. I wrote the amount in the budget book and slid the envelope behind the March tab.
You left the towel and those shoes in my back seat.
You want me to pull the car around before you leave for the center?
Thank you. I was still laughing about Clara sending hers backward.
Please. I have the ride slips and the Thursday lunch sheet, then First Baptist from 2 to 4.
Want me to check if it cleared later?
I heard y'all before I got to the door.
I put your newspaper clipping by the coffee pot.
Yes, but let me mark the little check box first. Then your screen and my book will match.
Thank you. I want to read that last part again before Paula calls tonight.
That was worth more than any number on that screen.
I will be ready. Come home after that and I will warm supper.
The part about more training?
That is the plan. I am not staying to set tables this time.
That, and the part saying the same rules ought to count for everybody wearing the badge.
At Ingles. Do we need meat for tonight?
No, come on home. I have soup started with the last frozen vegetables and a can of tomatoes.
Alright. Anything else?
Just the store brand milk. I will bake the cornmeal pan when you get back, and tomorrow I will use those peaches Paula brought.
Did you see the meal list I put on Facebook this morning?
I saw it after I left the center. I tapped the little bell and found your post.
Thank you. If you can add your soup under Thursday, that will help me keep count.
Done. The woman there also showed me how to turn off those pop-up notices.
Iris, Mrs. Halcomb posted another long note under the meal list, with that green tonic bottle and a donation button.
Please take my name off that reply chain. I will bring soup Sunday, but I am not answering that note.
I understand. I will keep you on the meal list only and leave the rest alone.
Miss Evelyn finished the last chapter early and wants to talk about the ending Tuesday.
I marked the page she mentioned. Could Ruth ride with me if the rain holds off?
She said yes. We can keep it to my porch afterward instead of joining the larger group at the diner.
That would be nicer. I will bring the oatmeal cookies and leave the diner table for the others.
Do you want me to drop the casserole dish by after Bible study, or will Frank be resting then?
Come by. He will be in his chair, and I will have the porch light on.
I still know which driveway is yours, even after all these years.
Same Covington driveway, just fewer cars in it now unless family is visiting.
I saved you a place beside me Sunday. Mrs. Elaine's husband asked for soup again, so I put us down for Tuesday.
That will be fine. Nights after visiting her make me count up our own papers and think too far ahead.
Bring the papers to church if you want me to look at the totals. We can keep it plain and simple.
Thank you. Paula said my portal still shows only the regular items, so I am trying to leave the rest until morning.
Mama, did Mrs. Carter ever answer you yesterday?
She did. Her phone was in the sewing room. I told her I would wave at Mr. and Mrs. Brown when I take the last tomatoes over.
Good. Please do not carry too much in one trip.
I will use the little basket. I still need to ring Miss Evelyn after lunch.
Mama, I can print those county pages at work before I leave. Which ones did you still need?
The school board comparison and the sheriff questionnaire, please. My copy is marked up around crosswalks, patrols near the park, and the senior clinic copays.
I will bring them Sunday. Do you want the grocery ad too?
Yes, especially meat and cereal. Frank and I are trying not to waste a dollar this week.
Mama, when you bring the folder Monday, please put the 1099 forms on top. The bank statement can go behind them.
I have three envelopes clipped together already. Social Security, the county plan, and the little interest paper.
That should be enough for the senior discount form. I will look it over after my lunch break.
Thank you. I will come by before the school traffic gets heavy.
Mama, did the plumber check clear yet? I can help you look at the online statement after work.
It cleared this morning. I already moved the grocery and pharmacy slips to the front of the folder.
Okay. Do you still want me to order the new curtains today?
Let us wait until May. I have enough in the house for meals, and the notebook will look better after April bills.
Do you want me to pick up new needles when I stop by Walmart after work?
Yes, size 9 if they have them. The last one bent on your daddy's shirt pocket.
Got it. Also Mia asked if you finished the pink bed top she saw on the chair.
Not finished. I pulled it out after breakfast and heard Mama telling me to slow down at the points.
I can bring the soup list by after Bible study Tuesday. Do you want me to come to the porch or just leave it in the mailbox?
Come to the porch if you have a minute. The azaleas finally opened and I want you to see them from the rocker.
I will. And I can move that big pot off the step while I am there.
That would help. Paula keeps fussing at me about clear steps, and she is not wrong.
Mama, I put the twins' garden pictures in the family folder. They want to know which seeds came from your back bed.
Tell them the zinnias are from the jar beside the flour canister. Those came from my mama's row by the porch.
They also asked why you always hum that same old tune when you water.
I heard it every Sunday before I was tall enough to see over the pew. Some things stay with your hands.
Are y'all still coming by after church next Sunday, or is there another Atlanta afternoon game Frank has circled?
Let me check his paper. He writes the times big so I do not promise us twice.
No rush. Mark said the New Orleans talk will pick up again soon, so I know Sundays get planned around the television.
That is about right. We can come early and be home before anything starts.
